paragraphs: Map the journey from the customer’s first finance enquiry to the lender or broker. Include online enquiries, telephone introductions, showroom conversations and any help with settling finance on a part-exchange. A label such as “we only introduce” does not settle the regulatory position.

A directly authorised dealership holds its own permissions and is responsible for complying with their scope and conditions. An appointed representative (AR) carries on the agreed activities under a principal’s responsibility. An AR arrangement is not unrestricted permission to conduct any finance activity.

An introducer appointed representative (IAR) has a narrower role, limited to introductions to its principal and distributing non-real-time financial promotions. Confirm the proposed activity with the principal before relying on this route.

A dealer owns its stock and plans to introduce buyers to third-party vehicle finance. The FCA’s motor-dealer guidance identifies limited-permission secondary credit broking as the likely route for that activity. If the dealer also takes part-exchanges with outstanding finance, additional permissions need consideration.
This example is a starting point, not a permission assessment for every dealership. Vehicle sourcing, non-owned stock and unrelated finance introductions can change the position.

social.ogDescription: Understand FCA authorisation, Firm Reference Numbers and permissions. Learn what to check on the Register before describing your dealership’s status.
social.twitterTitle: FCA Licence for Car Dealers: FRNs and Permissions | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Use the FCA’s official Register and search by the legal name or FRN. Match the entry to the business you are dealing with rather than relying on a copied logo or number.

Check the current status, the relevant permissions and restrictions, and any principal relationship. Read the entry’s details alongside the proposed activity. If something is unclear, use the FCA’s guidance or contact the firm through independently verified details.

Describe the dealership’s actual status accurately in customer communications. Do not treat authorisation as an FCA recommendation of the business or its products. An application in progress is not the same as approval.

For example, a dealer should not reuse a predecessor company’s regulatory wording just because the trading name and premises look the same. First establish which legal entity will carry on the activity.
Start with your business model and required activities, then prepare an application consistent with them. The application, website and customer process should describe the same business.
The FCA assesses the applicant firm. Support with documents does not transfer responsibility for understanding and explaining the application.

social.ogTitle: Limited vs Full FCA Permission: Motor Dealers | 009 Compliance

social.twitterTitle: Limited vs Full FCA Permission: Motor Dealers | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: These examples summarise the FCA’s motor-dealer guidance. They are not an exhaustive eligibility test. Consider all proposed regulated activities together.

The FCA sets separate conditions for finance introductions connected to a vehicle-sourcing service. These include whether the introduction would happen without that service and whether most revenue comes from sourcing rather than the credit introductions. Settlement of existing vehicle finance also affects the permissions to consider.
Introductions unrelated to the vehicles you sell, direct lending and hiring your own vehicles need their own assessment. Do not extend a permission conclusion from one business model to another.

“Limited” describes a permission category; it does not mean compliance ends when the application is approved. Customer communications, applicable Consumer Duty requirements, reporting and the firm’s permission limits still matter.
Prepare policies and processes proportionate to the actual business. A small dealership’s procedures can be practical and concise while still explaining who does what and how problems are handled.

Create a one-page activity map before choosing an application route. Record stock ownership, agreement types, partner firms, remuneration, part-exchanges and any separate lending or hire activity. Mark uncertainties for resolution before submission.
This is a suggested preparation method, not an additional FCA form. It helps make the business plan, application answers and website consistent.

social.twitterTitle: Credit Broking Permission for Motor Dealers | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Identify where the customer goes after asking about finance. A dealer that passes an enquiry to another broker still needs to consider its own regulated role. The CCR009 completion notes give examples of dealer introductions to finance providers and to intermediaries, whether or not a fee is earned.

If the dealership introduces a customer to a third-party lender, describe that role accurately. If a business also lends, its lending and broking roles need to be distinguished in the relevant communications.
An introduction is not a lender’s approval. Avoid wording that promises acceptance or implies every customer will receive finance.
Stock ownership and agreement types affect the limited/full-permission assessment. Helping with existing vehicle finance may introduce separate debt adjusting or counselling considerations.

Use the dedicated permission comparison rather than assuming that every dealership uses the same application. For AR or IAR arrangements, confirm the activity the principal has accepted and the limits of the appointment.

A buyer asks about finance for a vehicle. The dealer explains its role and passes the enquiry to a broker. That broker approaches a lender, which assesses the customer. The dealer should document its own steps, disclosures and responsibilities; the later involvement of a broker does not erase the dealer’s introduction.
This example illustrates the roles, not a universal compliant sales script. The required process depends on the arrangement and applicable rules.

social.ogTitle: FCA Application Documents: Motor Dealer Checklist | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Prepare motor-dealer FCA application documents: business plans, ownership and financial information, customer journeys, policies and pre-submission checks.
social.twitterTitle: FCA Application Documents: Motor Dealer Checklist | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Use this as a preparation checklist, then confirm the applicable forms and uploads in the FCA’s current guidance and Connect application. Not every item below is a separate mandatory upload for every dealer.

For a motor dealer, the FCA asks for an end-to-end customer journey, the intended lenders or brokers and the agreement types to be brokered. It also expects the risks and controls, how good customer outcomes will be delivered, Consumer Duty arrangements, fees and commission, and any unregulated activities to be explained.

Useful original detail includes a diagram of your own customer journey, the job role responsible for each step and how an exception is escalated. Avoid a generic plan that describes processes your staff will not actually use.

A complaints procedure should tell staff how to recognise, record and route a complaint. A vulnerable-customer process should describe the support staff can offer and when to ask for help. A promotions process should identify who approves wording and keeps the approved version.
These are examples of useful operational detail. Match each document to the firm’s actual obligations and scope; copying another dealer’s pack is not a substitute for checking applicability.

breadcrumbs.text: Why FCA Applications Get Delayed: A Motor Dealer Guide

social.ogTitle: Why FCA Applications Get Delayed | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Understand FCA assessment timescales, clarification requests and preparation checks for motor dealers. Learn what assistance can and cannot do.
social.twitterTitle: Why FCA Applications Get Delayed | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Allow for gathering information and resolving permission questions before submitting. That preparation period is distinct from the FCA’s assessment of the submitted application. A six-month assistance subscription is also a commercial commitment, not an FCA decision timetable.
The FCA may ask follow-up questions, request documents or hold a call or discussion. Approval depends on the application meeting the applicable standards.
The examples below are preparation checks, not a statistical ranking of delay causes.

A useful response process is to list each question, identify the supporting evidence and check that your answer is consistent with earlier material. Keep a record of what was sent and any requested response date.
If a business fact has changed, explain the change openly. The FCA warns that substantive changes indicating the firm is not ready may lead to a request to withdraw and reapply.

Administrative assistance can help organise information, prepare documents and coordinate responses. It does not remove the applicant’s responsibility or give a consultant control over the FCA’s decision.
The FCA expects the applicant to be accountable and able to explain the material. Preparing for a conversation means understanding your business and controls, not memorising a script.

paragraphs: The FCA confirms the activities, start date and any requirements or limitations in its decision. Make a practical record of these and share the relevant boundaries with staff. Do not assume an activity is permitted because it appeared in an early draft of the application.
This is an administrative plan, not a universal FCA rule requiring every item to be completed within 30 days. Follow any actual deadlines or conditions in the FCA’s correspondence.

Check whether CCR009 applies to the permissions held and review the schedule. Do not confuse collecting information each month with submitting the FCA return each month. A monthly internal process can help prepare for the applicable reporting cycle.

A new trading model, ownership change, additional finance activity or a different principal relationship may require action before it takes effect. Check the relevant FCA requirements rather than relying on the original application indefinitely.
Maintain a record of what changed, who checked its implications and what action was taken. This is a practical way to keep responsibility clear.

breadcrumbs.text: What Is CCR009? FCA Reporting for Motor Dealers

social.ogTitle: What Is CCR009? FCA Motor Dealer Reporting | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Learn what the FCA’s CCR009 return covers, which reporting it replaced and how motor dealers can prepare. Distinguish FCA filing from internal record collection.
social.twitterTitle: What Is CCR009? FCA Motor Dealer Reporting | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: The return covers permissions, the business model, marketing, revenue and staff. Questions are tailored to the activities and answers entered, so there is no single identical questionnaire that every dealership completes.
Start with the current form and completion notes. Use the FCA’s data-flow diagrams to understand the route through the questions that applies to your business.
CCR009 took effect on 7 May 2025. It replaced CCR004 and CCR005 and some information previously collected through CCR002 and CCR007. That does not mean every other scheduled return can be ignored.
Relevant limited-permission firms still submit CCR007 with reduced information alongside CCR009. Follow the current instructions for each scheduled return.

Use the questions to identify the source records you need, rather than guessing figures from total vehicle sales. Keep a note of the period, definitions and any calculations used. The return should describe the actual firm and the activity covered by the question.

Most firms report annually; a larger-firm exception applies. Your internal records can be updated more frequently to make preparation easier. Keeping monthly records does not turn CCR009 into a monthly FCA return.

social.ogTitle: Who Needs to Submit CCR009? | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Check CCR009 reporting scope for motor dealers, inactive firms, principals and appointed representatives using permissions and the firm’s actual schedule.

paragraphs: Match the legal entity and FRN to the permission record. Then review the actual reporting schedule and the relevant Handbook scope rules. Do not assume that another company in the same group, or a previous owner, has the same reporting position.

The CCR009 form provides for principal firms to include their own and their appointed representatives’ activity unless the question states otherwise. Where an AR has more than one principal, a principal reports the AR activity for which that principal is responsible.
An AR should agree what records its principal needs and when. Do not copy a directly authorised dealership’s filing process without checking the arrangement.

The form includes questions about use of permissions and expected activity. An empty commission ledger is not enough to decide that reporting can stop. Check the return’s instructions and describe the position accurately.

If the schedule appears inconsistent with the firm’s permissions or circumstances, raise the discrepancy with the FCA. Keep a record of the issue; do not assume that a query has cancelled or extended a deadline.

As a suggested administrative step, record the entity, FRN, permissions, principal relationships, returns shown and the person responsible for checking them. Review the record when the business changes.
This helps distinguish the question “does the firm report?” from “which questions does this firm answer?” The tailored questionnaire addresses the second question.

paragraphs: The table below is a preparation map, not a replacement for the full return or a claim that every category appears for every firm. Use the exact field wording, reporting period and any specified snapshot date when preparing the answer.

For each applicable field, record its reference, wording, definition, period or date, evidence location, calculation and preparer. Add a reviewer column if another person checks the work. This is a suggested working method, not an extra return to submit.
If a question’s meaning is uncertain, resolve it against the notes or with the FCA before entering a figure. Do not fill the gap with a total that happens to be available.

A dealer may hold a vehicle invoice, a finance agreement and a commission statement for the same transaction. These documents describe different amounts. Label each amount before deciding which record answers a particular return question.

For instance, a £12,000 vehicle sale, £10,000 credit amount and £200 commission are not interchangeable. These are fictional figures illustrating record separation, not instructions to place a particular amount in a particular field.

Complaints files, training evidence and monitoring records may be useful to the wider compliance process. Do not describe every internal record as a mandatory CCR009 submission item. Only the applicable form and its definitions determine what to enter.
Likewise, do not carry a calculation or proxy from another return into CCR009 unless its own instructions support that treatment.

Check the return’s final status and keep the confirmation after submitting. A useful internal record includes the version submitted, source records, preparer and date. Follow the firm’s applicable retention and data-protection arrangements.
If a submission error or unresolved discrepancy appears, investigate promptly. Do not describe the work as complete merely because the figures have been entered.

Mark each task complete, awaiting information or blocked. Assign an owner to every open item and deal with access problems early. A shorter, accurate checklist that somebody uses is more helpful than a long checklist nobody owns.

paragraphs: The FCA permits firms submitting CCR009 to report zero in CCR007 fields 1A and 3A where those fields relate only to credit broking or not-for-profit debt management. Where other limited-permission activities are carried on, accurate information for those activities is still needed. The remaining fields still require accurate information.
This is a specific concession, not permission to put zero everywhere or stop submitting CCR007. Check the current FCA instructions before relying on it.

CCR007 is a key-data return and can include complaints information for limited-permission firms. It should not simply be renamed “the complaints return”. Other complaints-reporting requirements depend on the firm’s scope.
Maintain the underlying complaints records and determine which reporting requirements apply. Do not assume that submitting CCR009 satisfies every other obligation.
Keep a separate line in the reporting calendar for each scheduled return, with its own period, deadline and owner. Link each answer to the correct return’s definition.

For a dealer with both returns, preparing one shared source-record pack can be efficient, but the answers must still be worked out separately. A rule or calculation used for CCR007 should not automatically be transferred to CCR009.

paragraphs: Two totals can look plausible while measuring different things. Write the field definition beside the source figure and explain any adjustments. If a number is unexpectedly different from the previous period, investigate the reason rather than changing it simply to make it look consistent.
Use the correct question period or date. A field asking for a snapshot cannot safely be answered with an annual total.

Identify the affected answer, the evidence and the corrected position. Check the current FCA process for correcting or resubmitting the data item, and contact the FCA if you cannot resolve the route. Keep a record of the issue and the action taken.

Do not submit a different return as a workaround or assume that changing an internal spreadsheet changes the filed return. This guide does not promise that every return can be corrected through the same screen.

A small firm can use a short exception log: issue, owner, evidence, resolution and date. Review the unresolved items before submission. Where another person checks the return, make the evidence easy for them to follow.

breadcrumbs.text: How to Prepare for a CCR009 Return

social.ogTitle: How to Prepare for a CCR009 Return | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Plan CCR009 preparation in stages: responsibilities, system access, source records, reconciliation, review and submission. Build an internal workflow for your firm.

paragraphs: The timetable below is a suggested internal workflow, not an FCA-prescribed preparation schedule. Set dates that leave room to resolve questions before your actual deadline.
The FCA says the firm’s Principal User has access to CCR009 and can grant other users the permissions needed to view, edit or submit it. Confirm the access each person actually needs.
Do not rely on sharing another person’s login. Keep responsibilities clear and make sure an absence does not leave the business unable to complete its reporting.

Start with the current form and completion notes. Create a list of applicable questions and ask each records owner for the relevant period and definition. This is more reliable than asking for “all finance figures” without explaining what is required.
Save an explanation of any calculation so the answer can be checked later. Mark unresolved questions rather than filling them with guesses.

Regular internal updates can make reporting easier. Choose a frequency that fits the business and its risks, then check that records remain complete and accessible. Monthly collection is an administrative choice, not a statement that CCR009 must be filed monthly.
After filing, note what caused difficulty and improve the next preparation cycle. An access issue, unclear definition or missing record can be assigned a specific action and owner.

social.ogTitle: When Is CCR009 Due? Periods and Deadlines | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Understand annual and six-monthly CCR009 reporting, the 40-business-day submission window and where to find your firm’s exact deadline.
social.twitterTitle: When Is CCR009 Due? Periods and Deadlines | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Sign in through the official My FCA portal and review the firm’s tasks and reporting schedule. Confirm the legal entity, data item, period and due date. Ensure the relevant user can access CCR009 in RegData.
If a return is missing or the details appear wrong, check user access and raise the issue with the FCA. Do not assume that not seeing a return proves it is not required.
CCR009 uses calendar-based periods, rather than the firm’s accounting reference date. A dealer with a different accounts year-end should map its records to the period required by the return.

For example, an annual filer with a September accounts year-end should not automatically use its October-to-September accounts totals for a January-to-December reporting period. This example explains period alignment; it is not a substitute for the firm’s actual schedule.

Set internal dates for gathering information, resolving questions, reviewing and submitting. Leave time for access problems and discrepancies. These internal target dates are suggested administration, not extra FCA deadlines.

If the deadline has been missed or submission is blocked, address it promptly with the FCA and retain a record of the issue. Do not assume a grace period or that raising a query automatically extends the deadline.

Where CCR007 is also required, manage it separately. Its submission period is 30 business days under the reporting table, compared with 40 for CCR009. Preparing both together does not make their deadlines interchangeable.

social.ogTitle: Consumer Duty for Motor Dealers | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Explore the four Consumer Duty outcomes for motor dealers, responsibilities by role, practical monitoring evidence, vulnerable-customer support and follow-up actions.
social.twitterTitle: Consumer Duty for Motor Dealers | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: These examples show possible evidence and actions. They are suggested ways to assess outcomes, not a mandatory list of documents or a complete compliance assessment.

A dealership distributing a lender’s product has a different role from the lender that designs it. That difference does not mean the dealership can ignore outcomes it influences. Identify what the firm controls, what it relies on partners for and how concerns are escalated.

The Duty’s cross-cutting obligations include acting in good faith, avoiding foreseeable harm and enabling and supporting retail customers to pursue their financial objectives. Apply the relevant rules to the actual service and customer journey.

A useful monitoring record sets out the issue, the evidence, which customers may be affected, the owner, the action and whether it worked. Use proportionate evidence from the business rather than collecting figures with no purpose.

For example, repeated questions about who provides finance may indicate unclear role wording. Review the wording, brief staff and check whether customers understand it better afterwards. This is an illustrative improvement cycle, not a claim that one test proves compliance.

Build a practical route for staff to recognise and respond to support needs. Consider communication preferences, time to understand information and escalation to an appropriate person. Avoid treating vulnerability as a single label that explains every customer’s needs.

The governing body’s review of retail customer outcomes is required at least annually under PRIN 2A.8.4R for firms within its application. A monthly internal check may help your business, but it is not a universal monthly reporting requirement under that rule.

social.ogTitle: Motor Dealer Website Compliance Checklist | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Review dealership status wording, finance promotions, commission disclosures, customer support and mobile readability using a practical checklist.
social.twitterTitle: Motor Dealer Website Compliance Checklist | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Use the checks below as a working review. Which disclosures and detailed promotion rules apply depends on the firm, its status and the communication.
If the firm only brokers credit, do not present it as the lender. If it is an AR, do not copy the status wording of a directly authorised firm. Do not describe a pending application as authorisation.

An example such as “We act as a credit broker, not a lender” can explain a broker-only role, but is not a complete disclosure template for every business. Check the entity, permissions, principal arrangement and other applicable requirements before publication.

CONC 4.5 sets conditions for disclosure of the existence and nature of commission or other remuneration, including where it could affect impartiality or the customer’s decision. Where that disclosure is required, the rules also address its possible effect on amounts payable. Amount or likely amount must be disclosed on request in the circumstances specified by the rules.

Review the actual arrangements and timing against the current rules. A generic footer sentence should not be treated as proof that all pre-contractual disclosure requirements have been met. This guide does not supply a universal commission clause.

Test whether a customer can tell who they are dealing with, what happens after an enquiry and where to obtain help. Distinguish financial-services disclosures from separate privacy and cookie obligations; this checklist is not a complete data-protection audit.

Keep a record of the pages reviewed, the changes made and the person approving them. Review again when the business model, permissions, partners or promotional terms change. Choose a proportionate routine review frequency rather than describing an arbitrary interval as an FCA requirement.

social.ogTitle: FCA Compliance for Motor Dealers: Guides | 009 Compliance
social.ogDescription: Find the right motor-dealer guide for authorisation, permissions, post-approval tasks, Consumer Duty, website checks and CCR009 reporting preparation and deadlines.
social.twitterTitle: FCA Compliance for Motor Dealers: Guides | 009 Compliance

paragraphs: Establish the legal entity, activities and relevant permission or principal arrangement before building the application. Make the business plan, website and customer journey consistent. The FCA expects the applicant to understand and explain the material submitted.

Check the permission conditions, brief staff and organise access to relevant systems. Monitor whether customers can understand the service and obtain the support they need. Keep evidence of issues, decisions and follow-up rather than treating compliance as a set of unused policies.

Begin with scope and the current schedule. Then map the applicable questions to source records, organise preparation and check submission. Internal monthly collection is an administrative method; the FCA filing frequency comes from the reporting rules.

A suggested internal calendar records each obligation or task, why it applies, the source of any deadline, the owner and the completion evidence. Separate recurring reporting from events triggered by a business change.

For example, reviewing a proposed new activity is different from completing an annual return. An ownership change, new permission requirement or change to a principal arrangement should be considered when proposed, rather than left until a routine review.

009 Compliance provides administrative assistance with authorisation, CCR009 returns and ongoing compliance work within the agreed scope. Motor-finance broker arrangements are a separate service to discuss. The dealership retains responsibility for its information, permissions and obligations.
